title: PITR from timestamp or position fails in a Kubernetes operator deployment
body: I am using Vitess v18.0.1 with the latest Vitess operator in Kubernetes. I take full backups with xtrabackup and incremental backups with the built-in method, with regular writes between backups. RestoreFromBackup fails when I try point-in-time recovery using a timestamp or position. I included a log gist from a failed timestamp restore.

symptoms_visible: RestoreFromBackup fails when I try to restore to a timestamp or position from my full and incremental backup chain in Kubernetes.
N0.label: N0 PITR restore failure reported

symptoms_visible: The shorter full-and-incremental backup flow fails during restore with 'mysqlbinlog command failed: exit status 1'.
Both my mysqld and vttablet containers have /usr/bin/mysqlbinlog on PATH.
N1.label: N1 failure reproduced and binary located

symptoms_visible: On the v19.0.0 cluster, restore still fails, and the expanded output says mysqlbinlog cannot find the requested file under /tmp/restore-incremental-.../vt/vtdataroot/.../bin-logs/.
N2.label: N2 mysqlbinlog stderr exposed

symptoms_visible: After the failed restore, neither container contains the restore-incremental directory under /tmp.
The mysqld and vttablet containers share /vt, while their /tmp contents differ, and the mysqld container restarts during restore.
N3.label: N3 container filesystem visibility established

symptoms_visible: With the image I built from the proposed changes, restore applies six incremental backups from paths under /vt/vtdataroot/restore-incremental-... and completes successfully.
N4.label: N4 candidate fix verified

symptoms_visible: Point-in-time restore successfully applies the incremental binlogs on a Kubernetes deployment using a build containing the restore-directory fix.
N_terminal.label: terminal PITR restore succeeds

question_patterns: Can you run the shortened full-and-incremental backup flow and report the exact restore result?
Does the same failure occur with the minimal backup script rather than your cron jobs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the shorter flow as well and got the same error. Restore fails while applying a binlog file and ends with 'mysqlbinlog command failed: exit status 1'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The shortened flow restores successfully; the failure only occurs with my original cron-job backup chain.
The shortened flow produces the same exit-status error on a different replica tablet.

question_patterns: Is mysqlbinlog installed and on PATH in the containers that run mysqld and vttablet?
Please run whereis mysqlbinlog and echo $PATH inside both the mysqld and vttablet containers.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In both the mysqld and vttablet containers, whereis reports mysqlbinlog at /usr/bin/mysqlbinlog. Their PATH includes /usr/bin.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: mysqlbinlog is not installed in either container.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c6 and c8: GenLN ran the maintainer's shortened flow on the same Kubernetes deployment, reproduced the error, and checked mysqlbinlog inside both containers. Localhost client tooling is not used as evidence about the restore process.

question_patterns: Can you retry with a build that includes the improved mysqlbinlog error output and paste the raw result?
Please deploy a version that exposes mysqlbinlog stderr, rerun RestoreFromBackup, and report exactly what it prints.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I retried on my v19.0.0 Kubernetes setup. The output says: "mysqlbinlog: File '/tmp/restore-incremental-3487966834/vt/vtdataroot/vt_0790125915/bin-logs/vt-0790125915-bin.000002' not found (OS errno 2 - No such file or directory)" followed by "ERROR: Could not open log file".

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The expanded output says mysqlbinlog cannot be executed because the binary is missing.
The same missing-file output names a different restore-incremental directory and binlog sequence number.

edges.comment: Reporter c12 after the diagnostic error-propagation work from c9-c11: GenLN changed the test cluster to v19.0.0 and supplied raw mysqlbinlog stderr. The answer reports only the missing path; the container-visibility diagnosis remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the relevant directories in both containers and report what files are present?
Please list /tmp and the tablet data directories after the failure, or run find on the restore directory if it is still present.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There is no restore-incremental folder or binlog file under /tmp in either container by the time I inspect it. The mysqld container's /tmp is empty, and the vttablet container only has unrelated files.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The exact requested binlog exists and is readable at the reported /tmp path inside the mysqld container.

question_patterns: Which filesystem paths or volumes are shared between the mysqld and vttablet containers?
Can both containers see the same tablet data directory, and are their temporary directories shared?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The mysqld and vttablet containers share /vt, so /vt/vtdataroot has the same content in both. Their /tmp directories do not show the same content.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both containers mount and see the same /tmp directory as well as the same /vt directory.
The shared volume is mounted at a custom path instead of /vt, but /tmp remains container-local.

edges.comment: Reporter c15: GenLN listed the mysqld and vttablet filesystems, stated that /vt is shared, showed differing /tmp contents, and volunteered that mysqld restarts during restore. Maintainer c16 explains cleanup timing, but that explanation is not placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Can you build and deploy the proposed test branch, rerun the backup and PITR flow, and tell me what happens?
Please test the proposed change in your Kubernetes cluster and paste the restore result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I built the image with the proposed changes and deployed it. I ran backups and then restored successfully. The log says it is applying six incremental backups, shows each binlog being applied from /vt/vtdataroot/restore-incremental-..., and completes the PITR restore.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate image still fails with the same missing file under /tmp.
The candidate image succeeds while applying a different number of incremental backups.

edges.comment: Reporter c27, following the test request in c21/c26: GenLN built and deployed the proposed Vitess image on the same Kubernetes setup. This is pre-landing candidate verification; the user reports successful application and the raw /vt/vtdataroot path without supplying the engineer's causal conclusion.

solution.intent: Use the tablet data root shared by the vttablet and mysqld containers for staging incremental-restore files, rather than a container-local /tmp directory, so mysqlbinlog can open and apply the extracted binlogs.
solution.concrete_example: Change the built-in incremental restore staging directory from /tmp/restore-incremental-* to a restore-incremental directory under /vt/vtdataroot (or the configured tablet root shared with mysqld), then use the successfully tested build for PITR.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the missing /tmp path, the container filesystem listings, the shared /vt mount, and the successful candidate-build logs. The conclusion that vttablet extracted the incremental binlog into a container-local temporary directory that mysqld could not see was made by the maintainer in c19 and confirmed by the candidate test.

edges.comment: Accepted diagnosis from c19-c28: the built-in restore extracted binlogs under a generated /tmp path visible to the Vitess-side container but not the mysqld container. GenLN verified the proposed shared-tablet-root change in c27. The official mysql image lacking mysqlbinlog, discussed in c29-c36, was explicitly separated into issue #15452 and is not part of this problem's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the built-in incremental restore staged binlogs under a container-local /tmp/restore-incremental-* path that was not visible to the separate mysqld container in the Kubernetes pod.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: mysqlbinlog was present, its raw stderr named a missing staged file, /vt was shared while /tmp was not, and the candidate build successfully applied binlogs from /vt/vtdataroot.
The fix must stage incremental-restore files under the tablet data root or another path shared by vttablet and mysqld, so mysqlbinlog can read them.
Must not treat the xtrabackup tmpdir setting as the fix; the failing path is generated by the built-in backup engine rather than the xtrabackup engine.
Must not conflate this restore visibility bug with the separate official-MySQL-image problem where mysqlbinlog is absent.
Must require successful PITR verification on the reporter's Kubernetes deployment using a build containing the shared-path change before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes and Vitess operator user who can inspect multi-container pods, collect detailed logs, build custom Vitess images, deploy test versions, and run backup and restore commands.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and highly detailed; provides command output, configuration excerpts, filesystem listings, and follow-up test results, while asking for clarification about build and deployment procedures.
